title: Annotatio III §.VIII Rescript: Private colloquies and letters abroad; procure church peace at least in Our realm
pass_a_gloss: Yours therefore, as Bishop and President of this whole Assembly, will be to make the named Men your Assessors more certain of Our most clement will declared by this Rescript, to meet and colloquy with them first within private walls without noise, and to act so that both by colloquies and by letters to be given to foreign Theologians valid means may be found by which Ecclesiastical Peace, longed for by the vows of all Evangelical Protestants, if not elsewhere, at least in Our Kingdom, Electorate, and other lands, may be procured and established.
pass_b_english: Yours, then, as Bishop and President of this whole assembly, will be to make those Assessors sure of Our most clement will declared in this Rescript.
Meet and confer with them first inside private walls, without noise.

See that — by colloquies and by letters to foreign theologians — solid means are found by which the church peace all Evangelical Protestants long for may be procured and settled, if not elsewhere, at least in Our Kingdom, Electorate, and other lands.
source_text: Tuum itaque, ceu Episcopi, totiusque hujus Consessus Praesidis, erit, nominatos Viros Assessores tuos de clementissima voluntate Nostra, Rescripto hoc declarata, certiores facere, cum iisdem, intra privatos primùm parietes, sine strepitu, convenire ac colloqui, idque agere, ut tùm per colloquia, tùm literas, ad extraneos Theologos dandas, valida media inveniantur, quibus Pax Ecclesiastica, omnibus Protestantium Evangelicorum votis exoptata, si non alibi, in Nostro saltem Regno, Electoratu exterisque terris, procuretur & stabiliatur.
notes: Private colloquy + foreign letters; peace at least in realm.
